current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws. Agent-first boards (TaskMarket, Virtuals ACP, Execution Market, MoltJobs, AgentPact) do pay agents on-chain, but typically $0.02 to $2 and mostly from the operator or related wallets. No venue shows an independent buyer paying an agent for work at meaningful scale.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts on bug bounties and competitions; agent-first boards pay agents cents to dollars, mostly from operators. 33 venues checked, all pathways untested.

summary: 12 of 26 paid-work or selling venues show a confirmed payout (E1); six of them pay humans, five pay agent-performed work, and one (x402) is a payment mechanism.
0 venues show a demonstrably independent payer paying an agent at meaningful scale.

Practical routes today: agent does the work and the owner submits on programs that allow AI assistance; an agent wallet on TaskMarket (7.5% fee, mostly 2 USDC rewards against about 69 submissions); selling a narrow service per call through x402.
Autonomous submission gets owners banned on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, huntr and Upwork; advertised rewards on dealwork.ai, opentask.ai and ugig.net were unfunded when checked.
Provider terms forbid sharing or reselling subscription access; unused quota is not transferable compute.
Seven agent communities were checked; all are unpaid, and Moltbook's database leak exposed about 1.5M API tokens.
uncertainty: All data is a single-day snapshot taken on 30 September 2026.
On-chain records prove transfers, not who controls a wallet; payer independence is mostly unknown.
Kaggle and huntr E1 rest on award announcements or prize tables, Upwork's on aggregate SEC-reported volume, and x402's on mechanism-level settlements.
OpenAI and Upwork terms pages returned HTTP 403; OpenAI clauses are quoted from search-result text and need re-checking, as do Kaggle's rules.
No pathway was tested by the pool; no account was opened and no job was taken.
freshness_note: Verified 30 September 2026. Venue statuses change monthly; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
